method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: Through the content lens this product is well above average and occasionally exceptional, but its quality is unevenly distributed in a way the baseline should record precisely. Wherever a human sat down and wrote a sentence, the writing is excellent and reader-side: the board's column subtitles ('Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision'), the Notes placeholder ('Write the thought before it disappears…'), Timeline's sharing disclosure ('Live since 15 Jul 2026. Anyone holding the link can read it.'), and the founder's note conceding that sprints and backlogs are genuinely useful. That last move — arguing against jargon without strawmanning it — is the most credibility-building thing on the site. Wherever a component needed a default string, the voice collapses to system-side filler: 'No tasks in this group', 'open source' as a link label, '4 milestones' with no verb, bare red dates carrying 'overdue' in colour alone. The gap between those two registers, not any single bad string, is the real finding. Two honesty issues deserve naming: Pricing opens with 'Start free' while its own trust band and every CTA on the site say waitlist-only, and Notes renders machine-transcribed voice and photo capture as clean prose with nothing marking it as transcribed. Neither is disqualifying, so I have issued no veto — there is no false price, no dark pattern and no broken flow — but the pricing contradiction is the highest-severity copy defect in the set. Attribution fails in mirror-image ways across the marketing pages: About runs an unsigned, undated note from 'the founder' while Pricing asks the reader to shape an Enterprise start 'with Ethan', a name introduced with no role; one fix repairs both. Finally, three limits on this score: axe returned zero violations everywhere and all pages returned 200 with no console errors, so nothing automated shaped my numbers; the marketing captures show only the top of each page, so body copy, footers, form and validation microcopy are unassessed; and no error state, no destructive-action confirmation, no share dialog and no failed-save message appears anywhere in the evidence. Error and edge-case wording is where content design is usually won or lost, and I have credited none of it.

surfaces.rationale: The board's column subtitles are genuinely best-in-class: 'Agreed and ready to start.', 'In motion right now.', 'Being checked before it goes out.', 'Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.', 'Finished work stays visible.' — each explains its column in the reader's terms, and 'Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision' is the kind of line most teams never write. The Waiting empty state reads 'Nothing held up', which is warm and specific. But the List view abandons that voice: the same empty group says 'No tasks in this group', which is system-side and uses 'group', a word the reader never chose. Worse, the board explains lateness in words ('Overdue by 2 days', 'Due today') while List shows only a red 'Due 14 Jul' / 'Due 16 Jul' with no word for overdue — the meaning moves entirely into colour, and the two views describe the same task differently. The desktop List priority column also truncates to unreadable fragments ('Hig', 'Low', 'No') at 1440px. Board and List are written by two different hands.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Bring List up to the board's voice: replace 'No tasks in this group' with the board's 'Nothing held up' phrasing, and put the overdue state into words in the Dates cell ('Overdue by 2 days') rather than leaving red type to carry it alone.

surfaces.rationale: The plain-language defaults are right — 'Mark done', 'No due date', "Doesn't repeat" instead of 'None', and an empty conversation that actually sets expectations: 'No conversation yet. Comments and changes will appear here as they happen.' The keyboard hint is a full sentence. Three real problems, though. The Source link reads 'From Notes · open source' — it means 'open the source note', but the string collides head-on with the software term and lands as nonsense; it is the most embarrassing single string in the app. Directly beneath it sits 'Approved wording: "Confirm marquee sides with hire company before Thursday"', a second and slightly different version of the task title with no explanation of what approved wording is, who approved it, or which version governs — a reader sees two titles and cannot tell which is real. And 'DRAFT A REPLY' offers machine-written text with a sparkle icon but no words anywhere saying it is generated or should be checked. 'Make copies' is also ambiguous about how many.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Rename the source link to 'Open the note' and either explain or remove the 'Approved wording' block — as it stands the detail panel shows the reader two competing versions of the same task title with no way to tell which one is authoritative.

surfaces.rationale: 'Write the thought before it disappears…' is the best microcopy in the product — it states the product's whole reason for existing in seven reader-side words. 'Private to you' with a lock, placed at the top of the surface, is a precise claim rather than a vague assurance. The row actions 'Keep / Turn into task / Delete' are three plain verbs, and 'Turn into task' is exactly right for someone who has never used a PM tool. The footer's 'Captured 35 minutes ago · Edited 31 minutes ago' plus the linked task underneath makes provenance visible. The honesty gap is the core mechanic: the mic-icon note ('Ask the venue whether the ballroom can be accessed from 8am on the Saturday.') and the photo note render as clean prose indistinguishable from typed text, with nothing saying it was machine-transcribed or that it may be wrong. Smaller cracks: the tab says 'Review' while the chip says 'To review'; the newsletter note truncates mid-quotation leaving an unclosed quote mark; the detail pane is mostly blank with no action copy.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Label transcribed voice and photo notes as transcribed, in words, with an invitation to correct them — right now machine-generated text is presented as if the user typed it.

surfaces.rationale: 'Live since 15 Jul 2026. Anyone holding the link can read it.' is the best sentence in the entire review set — it gives the state, the date and the actual consequence in the reader's own terms, where almost every product would have shipped 'Public link enabled'. The milestone states read 'Complete', 'Our next milestone', 'Coming up', 'Later' — plain, and the first-person plural is a deliberate register choice that suits a couple's shared page. 'Timing: 1 August 2026 · in 16 days' pairs absolute and relative correctly. Gaps: the disclosure names the exposure but never the undo, so a reader who dislikes what it says has no sentence telling them how to stop it; 'Preview' is a maker's word where 'See what guests see' would be the reader's; the Timeline product contains a view toggle also labelled 'Timeline', which is a naming collision with itself; '4 milestones' floats under a cluster of dots with no verb explaining whether it is a count, a range or a collapsed group; and filled/hollow/purple dots carry state with no text key. The share dialog, revoke confirmation and any error copy are not in the evidence, so I have given them no credit.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Pair the sharing disclosure with its undo in the same breath — 'Anyone holding the link can read it' should be followed by the plain sentence that tells the owner how to turn it off.

surfaces.rationale: The headline 'Project management for people outside tech.' is a real position rather than a slogan, and the subhead's antithesis — 'One calm system for people with work to manage, not software to manage' — is a genuinely good line that also names all three products in its first four words. Most valuable of all for trust: the CTA is 'Join the waitlist', not a fabricated 'Start free', which matches the app's own 'In development. You're seeing it early.' banner. Against that: 'See the system at work' is written from the vendor's side — 'the system' is not yet a concept the reader owns. 'Design' as a top-level nav item is opaque for an audience explicitly defined as outside tech. 'ONE THREAD, THROUGH THE STUDIO' is abstract and self-referential in a way the rest of the page's plain register is not. And the first screen makes a positioning claim with nothing beneath it to earn it — a large void sits between the eyebrow and the fold. Only the hero is captured; body sections, footer disclosures and any form microcopy are unassessed and I have credited none of them.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Rewrite 'See the system at work' from the reader's side — name the concrete thing they are about to be shown (the wedding the page actually follows) instead of asking them to care about 'the system'.

surfaces.rationale: This is the strongest writing on any surface here. The thesis — 'Project management software was built by tech companies, for tech companies.' — is arguable and specific rather than sloganeering, and the body does the rarest thing available in this genre: it names the vocabulary it objects to ('Sprints, epics, backlogs, story points, stand-ups and retrospectives') and then concedes those 'can all be useful when the work calls for them.' Refusing the strawman is the single most credibility-building move a founder's note can make. 'The mistake was assuming every project should work that way' is a narrow, defensible claim, and 'A wedding may be the largest project someone ever manages' ties the argument straight to the demo content in the app. The trust gap is attribution: the eyebrow promises 'A NOTE FROM THE FOUNDER' and the note is, on this evidence, unsigned and undated — an anonymous personal note undercuts the personal register it is trading on. On desktop the body paragraph is dropped into the right column beneath an empty left half, so the eye loses the thread between headline and argument.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Sign and date the note — give the founder a name and a face here, which also fixes Pricing's bare 'with Ethan' by making the reader already know who Ethan is.

surfaces.rationale: The intent is the best on the site and parts are genuinely rare: the trust band 'No charge / on the waitlist', 'VAT included / at the prevailing rate', 'Terms repeated / before purchase' puts three facts a buyer actually wants above the plans in plain words, and 'Terms repeated before purchase' is a checkable commitment most companies avoid making. 'Choose by the work in front of you.' beats 'Compare plans' outright, and 'Anything unresolved is named plainly' is a promise almost nobody makes. But the page contradicts itself on the one claim that matters most: the subhead opens 'Start free' while the band 100px below says 'No charge on the waitlist' and every CTA on the site is waitlist-only — so the reader cannot tell whether the product is available at all. 'Shape an Enterprise start with Ethan' names a stranger with no role or surname. And 'Pro' and 'Enterprise' are precisely the inherited industry vocabulary the About page's whole argument objects to, shipped unexamined. The plan cards and actual prices sit below the fold and are not captured, so the 'named plainly' promise cannot be verified and I have given it no credit.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Resolve the availability contradiction in the subhead — while the product is waitlist-only, 'Start free' must not be the first two words on the pricing page when the reassurance directly beneath it reads 'No charge on the waitlist'.
